verdict.rationale: Sill's documentation states there is no account and no server, so screen and keystroke traffic travels only between the user's own devices. Remote access away from home goes through the admin's own VPN (e.g. Tailscale) or a port forwarded on their router, so session traffic stays on infrastructure the admin runs by design. Missing for 10: there is no dedicated self-hostable relay or rendezvous component for NAT traversal (it relies on the admin's own VPN or port forwarding), and no independent or hands-on corroboration of the no-server claim.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the rendezvous or relay infrastructure so session traffic stays on infrastructure I run

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
